description: Prescribed burning of pastures and range land to control weeds and brush, has become a major, though potentially dangerous, management tool throughout Kansas.
credit: Paul D. Ohlenbusch, James W. Kunkel, Paul D. Ohlenbusch, James W. Kunkel, Prescribed Burning Safety, Kansas State University, Mar 1996.

credit: Dale F. Leikam, Dale F. Leikam, Using Legumes in Crop Rotations, Kansas State University, Oct 2007.

title: Weedy Bromes-Recognizing Them at an Early Stage
description: Identifying weedy bromes (vs. wheat or smooth brome) at an early state is difficult, but with a hand lens it is possible to observe type of ligule, edge on leaf blade, & distribution of hairs. Photos.
credit: Linda W. Davis, Linda W. Davis, Weedy Bromes-Recognizing Them at an Early Stage, Kansas State University, May 1990.

title: No-Till Alfalfa Establishment after Small-Grain Cereals
description: A major concern in alfalfa production is stand establishment. In Kansas, most alfalfa is planted during August. With no-till alfalfa planting, more moisture is often available for germination.

description: Grain sorghum in Kansas often is subjected to a killing freeze before maturity. It is crucial to make a test cutting, analyze it for test weight, yield potential before making any decisions.

title: Quality Oriented Marketing of Hard Winter Wheat

title: Predicting the Final Irrigation for Corn, Grain Sorghum, and Soybeans
description: To schedule final irrigation, the following information is needed: Current crop stage of growth. Predicted water use to maturity. Amount of usable water in root zone. Assume no rain occurs.

description: Triticale generally has higher forage yields, but lower quality than wheat, especially when harvested as hay or silage. It has similar crude protein values (20-25%) as wheat when grazed.
credit: James P. Shroyer, Robert L. Bowden, Ray E. Lamond, James P. Shroyer, Robert L. Bowden, Ray E. Lamond, Triticale in Kansas, Kansas State University, Oct 1996.

title: Impact of Climate, Disease, and Wheat Breeding on Wheat Variety Yields in Kansas, 1985-2011
description: This research quantifies the impact of climate change, disease, and genetic improvement on wheat yields of varieties grown in 11 locations in Kansas from 1985-2011. Variety yield data from Kansas performance tests were matched with comprehensive location-specific weather and disease data. Results show that wheat breeding programs increased yield by 0.51 bu/acre each year, and a 1ºC increase in projected mean temperature decreases yields by 10.64 bu/acre. 36 pages.
